title: Queue Harmonizer for Heterogeneous Token Workloads and Adaptive Attention Pacing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: tail latency spikes persist on multi-tenant GPU pools when short interactive requests mix with long prefill-heavy streams. Existing admission heuristics either over-prioritize short queries (starving decode progress) or overly-constrain throughput, causing customer-visible latency regressions. This ticket proposes a Queue Harmonizer: a runtime component that regulates slot admission and attention execution pacing across heterogeneous token-length mixes. The Harmonizer combines probabilistic slot preemption, progressive attention pacing (soft governor on attention compute for long prefill bursts), and a micro-batching reshaper to reduce tail quantiles while preserving aggregate throughput.
acceptance_criteria: P95 end-to-end generation latency reduced by >= 28% on mixed workload benchmark compared to baseline (runtime-1.20) under 50% short / 50% long token distribution
Throughput (tokens/sec) loss <= 5% versus baseline under steady-state heavy load
No customer-visible errors or increased OOMs in integration cluster for 72h smoke run
Feature gated behind harmonizer.enabled and default-off for Dedicated until experimental flag opt-in
implementation_notes: Introduce harmonizer module in admission pipeline between queue and slot allocator
Maintain per-tenant token-length histograms and short/long moving-window counts for adaptive thresholds
Probabilistic slot preemption: when queue congested, preempt a fraction of long-prefill slots (gradual, ranked by age and decode progress) and re-allocate to short interactive requests
Progressive attention pacing: add a soft token-rate governor that reduces attention compute budget for long prefill windows to avoid kernel monopolization; ramp back once short-query backlog clears
Micro-batch reshaper: coalesce small short queries into temporary micro-batches when possible to reduce kernel startup overhead without increasing latency beyond a configured SLO
Expose tuning knobs: long_token_threshold, preempt_fraction_max, pacing_decay_ms, microbatch_max_delay_ms
Ensure compatibility with kernel selection: harmonizer informs kernel-planner about expected batch shapes for improved kernel choice
Instrumentation: emit per-tenant harmonizer decisions, preemption counts, pacing events, and microbatch latencies to console and perf dashboards
testing_plan: Unit tests for harmonizer decision logic (stateless determinism under fixed seeds)
Integration tests on staging with synthetic mixed workloads (short=8-32 tokens, long=512-2048 tokens) including rollout canary
A/B against baseline runtime-1.20 for 48h with traffic replay from production traces
Fault-injection: simulate stalled decodes and verify preemption does not deadlock slots
Load test on Dedicated with reserved capacity to validate throughput and OOM behavior
risks: Aggressive preemption could starve long-running batch jobs and reduce overall token throughput if mis-tuned
Pacing changes may interact with quantized-kernel performance and reduce efficiency for certain models
Increased complexity in admission pipeline could make root cause analysis harder without good observability
Feature turned on by default risks unexpected behavior for customers using fixed-capacity Dedicated clusters
rollout_strategy: Feature gated; start with internal staging clusters
Canary rollout: 1% of runtime traffic with synthetic mixed workload -> 10% -> 25% -> 100% over several days if metrics stable
Automatic rollback if latency.p95 increases by >10% or preemption rate correlates with errors
Gradual enable in Dedicated as opt-in config for first 30 customers
